Definition: adverb from G146; sordidly:--for filthy lucre's sake.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in Peter's charge to the elders: Feed the flock of God which is among you, not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind. The word is the adverb — how the work is done.
TheologicalSignificance: One adverb in one verse carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Peter's test of the shepherd's motive, whether the work would go on if the pay stopped.
